numeric.name: driver_age
numeric.description: Age of the primary driver in years; a core risk factor capturing young/inexperienced and elderly driver risk profiles.

numeric.name: vehicle_age
numeric.description: Age of the insured vehicle in years; older vehicles typically have lower values but higher mechanical failure risk and different repair cost profiles.
numeric.data_quality_note: Max of 68 years is plausible for classic vehicles but worth validating; no nulls.

numeric.name: age_driving_licence
numeric.description: Number of years the driver has held a licence; proxy for driving experience, inversely related to risk for younger drivers.
numeric.data_quality_note: Min of 0 may indicate newly licensed drivers or a data entry issue; should be cross-checked against driver_age.

numeric.name: vehicle_value
numeric.description: Market or insured value of the vehicle; key driver of property damage and theft premium adequacy.
numeric.data_quality_note: 0.14% nulls; max of ~374k suggests high-value outliers — consider capping or log-transformation. Imputation needed for missing values.

numeric.name: power_to_weight_ratio
numeric.description: Ratio of engine power to vehicle weight; higher values indicate sportier, higher-risk vehicles.
numeric.data_quality_note: Min of 0 may indicate missing or electric vehicles with no combustion engine — verify zero values are valid.

numeric.name: seats
numeric.description: Number of seats in the vehicle; proxy for vehicle category (passenger car vs. minibus) and occupant exposure.
numeric.data_quality_note: Low cardinality (8 unique values); could be treated as categorical but numeric treatment is acceptable.

numeric.name: liability_exposure
numeric.description: Fractional exposure period for liability coverage; captures partial-year policies and adjusts for time at risk.
numeric.data_quality_note: Min of 0.0027 is very small but plausible for short-term policies; no nulls.

categorical.name: policy_type
categorical.description: Type of motor insurance policy (e.g., comprehensive, third-party); directly determines coverage scope and expected premium level.
categorical.data_quality_note: No nulls; 5 categories with some low-frequency levels (TP: 5,757) that may need grouping.

categorical.name: business_type
categorical.description: Indicates whether the policy is new business (NB) or a renewal/portfolio transfer (P); renewal business typically has lower risk due to selection effects.

categorical.name: payment_frequency
categorical.description: Frequency of premium payment (Annual, Semi-annual, Quarterly); may correlate with policyholder financial profile and lapse risk.
categorical.data_quality_note: Q has relatively low frequency (15,395); may be grouped with S.

categorical.name: bonus_score
categorical.description: Bonus-malus or behavioural score category (Good, Neutral, Bad); direct indicator of historical claims behaviour and future risk.
categorical.data_quality_note: N and B categories are low frequency (7,850 and 4,730 respectively); monitor for credibility.

categorical.name: fuel_type
categorical.description: Type of fuel used by the vehicle (Diesel or Gasoline); associated with vehicle usage patterns, mileage, and repair costs.
categorical.data_quality_note: 0.36% nulls; imputation or a separate 'Unknown' category required.

categorical.name: vehicle_brand
categorical.description: Manufacturer brand of the insured vehicle; captures brand-level differences in repair costs, theft attractiveness, and safety ratings.
categorical.data_quality_note: 68 unique brands; many low-frequency brands will require grouping. No nulls.

categorical.name: municipality_type
categorical.description: Classification of the municipality where the vehicle is garaged (e.g., inner city, city, suburban/island); captures urban density and traffic risk.
categorical.data_quality_note: IS category is low frequency (24,137); consider merging with C or I depending on risk profile.

categorical.name: circulation_area
categorical.description: Whether the vehicle primarily circulates in urban (U) or rural (R) areas; urban areas typically have higher frequency but lower severity claims.
